author: human
request:
Bug report: opening /owners?page=0 — or any page value below 1 — renders the
error page instead of the owner list. Expected behavior: the owner listing
treats any page value below 1 as the first page and responds with the normal
listing (HTTP 200). Find the cause, fix it, and cover the fix with a test.

title: Owner listing shows the first page when a page before the first is asked for

acceptance_criteria: given owners to list, when a page before the first is asked for, then the first page of owners is listed
given owners to list, when a page before the first is asked for, then the listing is shown rather than the error page

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The owner listing's paging stays exactly where it is; one adjustment lands inside OwnerController. architecture-principles.md Pattern Catalog, Web controller row, already states that normalizing a request parameter to its permitted range is binding rather than a business rule, so this fix adds no fresh violation of that row and needs no new type, package, or seam. The adjustment: processFindForm normalizes the bound page parameter to the first page when a page before the first is asked for, ahead of both findPaginatedForOwnersLastName and addPaginationModel. Placement ahead of both is load-bearing, not cosmetic: owners/ownersList.html builds its next, previous, first, and last links from the currentPage model attribute (lines 35-56), so clamping only inside the query helper would list the first page while rendering a page marker and a next link derived from the un-normalized value. system-design.md Contracts now records REQ-OWN-005 on the OwnerController row and a Paging on the owner listing paragraph states the normalization and the veterinarian divergence. Basis for the covering-pattern claim is grep over docs/architecture-principles.md and the two controllers plus a read of OwnerController and the template, not the IDE oracle, which is not connected in this run; that is the weaker basis.
integration_points: Repository boundary (OwnerRepository): the test crosses it through the @MockitoBean OwnerRepository field OwnerControllerTests already declares. No new double is introduced — the new case reuses the class's existing seam and stubs findByLastNameStartingWith as its siblings do (OwnerControllerTests:146-148). A hand-written OwnerRepository double is not chosen: the Spring Data interface inherits the whole CRUD and paging surface, so hand-writing it would add roughly twenty unused methods to serve one assertion. testing-principles.md Mocking Policy admits this as the conscious framework-stub exception; the existing suite's usage is the ceiling, not an invitation to widen it.

Framework transport (HTTP): MockMvc, the one sanctioned mock per CLAUDE.md Testing Strategy and testing-principles.md Mocking Policy. It drives the real MVC dispatch and the real int binding of the page parameter, which is what makes the error-page-versus-listing assertion meaningful.

View model: owners/ownersList.html reads currentPage and totalPages. The normalized page must reach addPaginationModel, so a request for a page before the first renders a page marker and navigation links for the first page.
Entry point: no new one. GET /owners already exists, its Owner command-object binding is unchanged, and the @InitBinder disallowing id and *.id stays as is. No new binding target to name.

patterns.description: Pattern Catalog, Web controller row: normalizing a request parameter to its permitted range or shape is binding, not a business rule. This is the row that authorizes the fix inside the controller

A new business rule in a controller is a fresh violation not covered by the existing deviation. The distinction the paragraph draws — a parameter's range belongs to the request that carries it — is why this adjustment stays clear of that line
findPaginatedForOwnersLastName, the existing pagination helper holding PageRequest.of(page - 1, pageSize); page 0 yields index -1 and Spring Data rejects it
Existing multi-case paging test in the same class, looping its cases over one stubbed page. The nearest shape for the data-driven test the prd-entry names, with edge cases 4 and 5 as its cases

risks.risk: The owner listing's paged query is the one path here that scales with data. docs/system-design.md carries no Scale and Load section, so no row exists to cite.
risks.mitigation: The slice adds no path and changes neither page size nor access pattern — it only changes which page index an out-of-range request resolves to, and the query stays the same single paged prefix search. Size and access pattern are therefore unrecorded and treated as bounded, and the simplest readable form (the existing derived paging query) is the recorded design. No row is written: foundation is demand-driven and this slice does not touch the load question.

risks.risk: Normalizing inside findPaginatedForOwnersLastName instead of at the entry point would satisfy the first Done-when bullet (the first page is listed) while leaving currentPage un-normalized in the model, so owners/ownersList.html would render a page marker matching no page and a next link one past the un-normalized value. A test asserting only the view name and the listed content would pass.
risks.mitigation: Normalize once where the parameter is bound, in processFindForm, and pass the normalized value to both the query and addPaginationModel. Assert the rendered currentPage, not only the view name. This is the Web controller row's own placement (docs/architecture-principles.md:85): binding happens at the surface that binds.

risks.risk: The veterinarian directory carries the identical expression at VetController:61 and stays broken. A reader or a later slice may read the divergence as an oversight and widen this fix.
risks.mitigation: Out of scope by the prd-entry's non_goals and recorded as an open question in docs/prd.md Open Questions. docs/system-design.md now states the divergence and points at that question, so the current state is readable without re-deriving it. The implementer touches no file under vet/.

risks.risk: A page after the last, and a page that is not a number, are both out of scope. A normalization written as a general two-sided clamp would silently take the upper bound too, shipping behavior no requirement covers.
risks.mitigation: Normalize the lower bound only. docs/prd.md Open Questions and the prd-entry's non_goals are the bar; REQ-OWN-005's Done-when bullets and edge cases 4 and 5 are the whole target.

notes: Five-signal foundational check: none trips. The design doc carries confirmed statements, ADRs record both the framework choice (2026-07-31-java-17-and-spring-boot) and the architecture shape (2026-07-31-feature-package-organization, 2026-07-31-server-side-rendering-with-thymeleaf), docs/ubiquitous-language.md carries confirmed domain terms, the project-level concern this slice touches (request-parameter handling at the web boundary) has its pattern recorded in architecture-principles.md, and no new bounded context appears. No ADR written: the placement decision is already recorded in the pattern catalog and the tolerate-rather-than-refuse decision is already recorded in docs/prd.md as an answered question, so per adr-template there is no trade-off a later reader would re-litigate. Paging is a presentation concern and adds no ubiquitous-language term; prose follows the PRD's wording — the owner listing, a page before the first. No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit skipped. docs/system-design.md edits are the two named above and nothing else. python3 scripts/doctor.py check passes, 0 failures, with the REQ-OWN-005 citation now resolving.

author: change-grader
summary: clamp the owner-listing page parameter to the first page

blast_radius.note: One expression in one method of one controller, nine production lines in a single module, no sensitive or security-surface paths; the only downstream consumer is the ownersList template's currentPage links, and the change keeps that value coherent with the query.

semantic_surprise.note: Math.max(page, FIRST_PAGE) does exactly what the comment and PRD prose claim: pages at or above one pass through untouched, and the normalized value feeds both findPaginatedForOwnersLastName and addPaginationModel, so the trap of normalizing the query while leaving currentPage at zero is avoided; the unnormalized upper bound and non-numeric page binding are pre-existing and untouched.

test_adequacy.note: The new parameterized test genuinely exercises the changed behavior for page 0 and -3, asserting the rendered currentPage and capturing the Pageable to prove the query saw page index zero, but no test in the class passes any other page value, so a clamp written as a flat FIRST_PAGE that pinned every request to the first page would leave the whole suite green.

reviewer_hedging.note: Three approvals with zero findings and a reasoned security-reviewer exclusion the plan recorded, so the silence is expected; the single recommendation is parked polish about the duplicated first-page literal, not a correctness reservation, and although the doc-reviewer's line numbers are stale, every claim it cited was re-verified true at its actual location.

scope_deviation.note: Zero build retries, consultations, and design revisions; the diff touches only the owner listing's page handling and the two docs that describe it, and the adjacent veterinarian paging was deliberately left alone and recorded as an open question rather than silently fixed.

rationale: The clamp is correct and both consumers receive the normalized page, so the residual risk sits in the suite rather than the code: nothing anywhere asserts that a valid page above the first still reaches the query. Read OwnerController.java:109 and confirm Math.max, not a constant.
